messages.author: dbc05514efb8c1db
messages.subject: Settin up a Poisson regression in stan
parts:
Hi all,

I'm new to stan programming. I'm trying to adapt a script written for JAG to STAN. I'd like to convert  T[i] <- step(yrep[i]-y[i]) - 0.5*equals(yrep[i],y[i]) in the stan format. I'm getting the following error when I compile my code:

> HiC_code <- '
+   data {
+     int<lower=1> K;
+     int<lower=1> N;
+     matrix[N,K] x;
+     vector[N] y;
+   }
+   parameters {
+     matrix [K,1] beta;
+   }
+    transformed parameters {
+     vector[N] theta;
+     theta <- rows_dot_product(beta,x);
+    }
+   model {
+     for(i in 1:N){
+       y[i] ~ poisson_log(theta[i]);
+     }
+     for(j in 1:K){
+       beta[j] ~ normal(0,0.001);
+     }
+   }
+   '
> HiC_data <- list(N=nrow(X),K=ncol(X),y=dat$u_vec,x=X);
> fit <- stan(model_code = HiC_code, data = HiC_dat, iter = 1000, chains = 4);

Yes, this one is easy. Replace:
y[i] ~ poisson_log(theta[i]);

with:
y[i] ~ poisson(theta[i]);


If you want more info, page 315 of the manual. You can also vectorize (if that's easier to understand). You can remove the loop:
for (i in 1:N) {
  y[i] ~ poisson(theta[i]);
}

with this vectorized call:
y ~ poisson(theta);




Daniel

Wouldn't it be better as a generated quantity, since it doesn't affect the log probability?

Also, Stan has other ways of constraining parameters to be positive, if that's all the theta transformation is doing. And there's probably a cleaner way to tackle those n-by-1 matrices...

And depending on where you're at numerically, you
are probably better off with the log-scale parameterization,

poisson_log(x * beta)

I think the "matrix[K,1]" should all be "vector", too.
Then (x * beta) is an n-vector. You can still save (x * beta),
but I'd put that (theta) in the generated quantities --- not sure
if that's what Ken Arnold meant.

- Bob

messages.author: 20758fda448fdbda
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Settin up a Poisson regression in stan
parts: If I understand your model correctly, yrep is not really a parameter but another "y-type" random variable generated with the same theta that is found for "y". Also, T is a quantity of interest, not a part of the model per se. The data is N, K, x, and y and beta is an "unknown" parameter. As  such, perhaps the following model would work for you:

data {
  int<lower=1> K;
  int<lower=1> N;
  matrix[N,K] x;
  int y[N];
}
parameters {

vector[K] beta;
}
transformed parameters {
  vector[N] theta;

theta <- exp(x * beta);
}
model {

y ~ poisson(theta);
  beta ~ normal(0, 1000);
}
generated quantities{
  vector[N] T;
  int yrep[N];
for (i in 1:N) {
yrep[i] <- poisson_rng(theta[i]);

T[i] <- step(yrep[i] - y[i]) - 0.5 * if_else(yrep[i] == y[i], 1, 0);
  }
}

Using some random data
set.seed(875)
DATA <- list(K = 5, N = 10, x = matrix(rnorm(50, 5, 1), ncol = 5), y = sample.int(n = 25, size = 10))

The second model ran a bit faster and did not throw the sampling error as yrep is neither a transformed paramater nor sampled any longer. Also, you now get the Yreps and T's as outputs.

Hope that helps.

On Tuesday, April 8, 2014 6:12:19 AM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
And depending on where you're at numerically, you
are probably better off with the log-scale parameterization,

   poisson_log(x * beta)

I think the "matrix[K,1]" should all be "vector", too.
Then (x * beta) is an n-vector.  You can still save (x * beta),
but I'd put that (theta) in the generated quantities --- not sure
if that's what Ken Arnold meant.

- Bob

On Tue, Apr 8, 2014 at 1:15 AM, Ken Arnold <kcar...@seas.harvard.edu> wrote:

Wouldn't it be better as a generated quantity, since it doesn't affect the log probability?

Ah, yes, of course.  I thought T was being used elsewhere in the model.

Cheers,
Marcus

Also, Stan has other ways of constraining parameters to be positive, if that's all the theta transformation is doing. And there's probably a cleaner way to tackle those n-by-1 matrices...

On Mon, Apr 7, 2014 at 6:05 PM, Mark Carty <mac...@cornell.edu> wrote:
Hi all,

Thanks for the advice. I was able to get it run. I'd like to extract the T[i]'s from the model, which written below. How do I accomplish this?.

  data {
    int<lower=1> K;
    int<lower=1> N;
    matrix[N,K] x;
    int y[N];
  }
  parameters {
     matrix[K,1] beta;
  }
  transformed parameters {
    matrix[N,1] theta;
    theta <- exp(x * beta);
  }
  model {
    int yrep[N];
    real T[N];
    for(i in 1:N){

      y[i] ~ poisson(theta[i]);
      yrep[i] ~ poisson(theta[i]);
      T[i] <- step(yrep[i]-y[i]) - 0.5*if_else(yrep[i]==y[i],1,0);
    }
    for(j in 1:K){
      beta[j,1] ~ normal(0,1000);

    }
  }


If you declare T in the transformed parameters block (like theta), they will be saved out with the other parameters.

Cheers,
Marcus
